## Shipping release `v<VERSION>`

**Do not merge this PR directly.** The conductor keeps this branch (`release-prep/<REL_BRANCH>`) force-pushed on every push to `<REL_BRANCH>` — any commits made here (including a hand-merge) are silently overwritten on the next conductor run. Instead:

1. **Mark this PR ready-for-review** (out of draft) and approve it.
2. **Trigger the [ship-release workflow](../../actions/workflows/ship-release.yml)** via `workflow_dispatch` — pick `version` = `<VERSION>`, `rel_branch` = `<REL_BRANCH>`, and `mode` (default `semi-auto`, or `full-auto`, or `dry-run`).

Ship-release then handles the annotated-tag creation, the paired `release-finalize/<REL_BRANCH>` master-side PR merge, and (in `full-auto` mode) the `release-docs/<VERSION>` website PR merge — see [RELEASE_PROCESS.md § Quick action 3 — Ship the release](../../docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md#3-ship-the-release) and the full runbook for the mode semantics, guardrails, and the recovery paths if any downstream step stalls.

- **Docker acceptance** — [acceptance-docker.yml runs on `release-prep/<REL_BRANCH>`](../../actions/workflows/acceptance-docker.yml?query=branch%3Arelease-prep%2F<REL_BRANCH>): `fresh-install-from` + `fresh-install-to` + `upgrade` scenarios against the image built from this branch's `docker/release/Dockerfile`.
